title: Tapirscan documentation
description: Use the Tapirscan barcode scanner in JavaScript, Python and native applications.

sections.title: Scan locally
sections.text: Tapirscan detects multiple barcodes and returns their values, formats and positions. Browser and Node applications use Rust/WebAssembly; Python uses native libraries. Images stay in your application.

sections.title: Other language bindings
sections.text: Rust, C, C++ and Java bindings share the scanner core. Follow each guide for build and platform requirements.

sections.title: For coding agents
sections.text: Use the documentation for your installed version. The next demo builds can be newer than the published packages. Supported linear and 2D formats are listed in the format guide; Turbo presets remain experimental. Use the Markdown exports for compact documentation; AGENTS.md describes repository development, not the public API.

title: Barcode scanning with JavaScript and TypeScript
description: Install Tapirscan for browser and Node.js applications, load WASM assets and reuse a scanner.

sections.title: Install
sections.text: Node.js 20+ is required by the package. The runtime must support WebAssembly SIMD. TypeScript declarations and WASM files are included.

sections.title: Browser quick start
sections.text: In browser apps, tapirscan/browser accepts files, images, video frames and canvases and scans in a bundled worker. These examples use the 1.3.0 API; older releases have a different result model.

sections.title: Reuse a scanner
sections.text: Construct a scanner synchronously and await each scan. Reuse it for repeated images or camera frames; dispose it when finished.

sections.title: Node.js inputs
sections.text: The default Node loader reads packaged WASM files. Decode PNG/JPEG files with an image library before calling scan: encoded bytes and filenames are not pixel inputs.

sections.title: Camera and worker integration
sections.text: The browser entry handles worker setup and image capture. Await each scan in a camera loop to avoid a queue of stale frames. Call inspect instead of scan when you need timing, unread regions or work status. Vite 6/7 development servers need optimizeDeps: { exclude: ["tapirscan"] }; see the complete guide for bundler setup.

title: Barcode scanning with Python
description: Read barcodes from Pillow images, NumPy arrays and tensors with Tapirscan.

sections.title: Install
sections.text: Python 3.10+ is required. Available platform wheels include native scanner libraries. Install Pillow for the following example.

sections.title: Scan a photo
sections.text: Medium effort and the Retail format group are the defaults. Barcode coordinates refer to the input image.
sections.code:
from PIL import Image
import tapirscan

with Image.open("label.jpg") as image:
    barcodes = tapirscan.scan(image, mode="medium", formats="retail")

print([barcode.text for barcode in barcodes])
for barcode in barcodes:
    print(barcode.text, barcode.format, barcode.polygon)

sections.title: Arrays and repeated scans
sections.text: The library also accepts supported NumPy arrays, tensors and explicit pixel buffers. Check the complete guide for dtype, channel layout, stride, device and ownership requirements. Use a reusable Scanner when scanning many images. Call inspect for a report with timing, unread regions and work status. These examples use the 1.3.0 API; follow the migration guide when upgrading from 1.2.2.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.text: If no wheel matches your platform, follow the native build instructions. Install only the optional image libraries you use. Select the formats you need and check the format guide for supported variants and limitations.

title: Barcode formats and scanning effort
description: Supported Tapirscan barcode formats, format presets, variant limitations and four effort modes.

sections.title: Supported formats and variants
sections.text: Tapirscan supports linear and 2D barcode formats. EAN13, UPCA, EAN8 and UPCE are enabled by default; select additional formats as needed. Inclusion in a preset does not guarantee every barcode of that format will decode.

sections.title: Format presets
sections.text: Preset names are case-sensitive. Retail is the default. Enable the formats you need: broader selections may require more work.

sections.title: Effort modes
sections.text: Choose low, medium, high or very-high. Medium is the default. Higher effort permits more search; it does not guarantee a read or lower latency on any particular image. These are scanner effort modes, not downloadable neural models.

sections.title: Results and limitations
sections.text: Multiple symbols can be returned. A missing read is not proof that an image has no barcode. Empty result arrays mean no barcode was decoded. Read completion and work-limit diagnostics when making decisions about partial scans.

title: Tapirscan releases and demo builds
description: Understand published Tapirscan packages and the newer next builds used by the interactive demo.

sections.title: Published packages
sections.text: These guides describe version 1.3.0. Check npm and PyPI for available releases and use the tagged guide for your installed version. Package releases and website deployments are separate operations.

sections.title: Current demo preview
sections.text: The source checkout’s next readers follow the selected release candidate. Current Turbo comparisons are pinned separately. The deployed demo may differ until it is rebuilt and published. Check the version selector and engine identity for the build you are using.

sections.title: Version identity matters
sections.text: Do not assume a demo preview is already available from npm or PyPI. Use release tags for released API documentation. For reproducible comparisons, record the scanner build, active formats, effort mode, image transformations and device. No new comparative performance claims are published on this page.

sections.title: License packaging correction
sections.text: Version 1.3.0 package inputs include the full MIT and Apache 2.0 texts, correcting the license-file mismatch in 1.2.2. See the license page for details. Website deployment does not replace published package artifacts.
